outer_batch_active.meaning: a top-level multicall batch is executing and its outer loop has not finished
outer_batch_active.checkpoint: before the subsequent outer payload is processed

inner_payload_calls_multicall.meaning: a payload within the batch invokes multicall again (nested multicall)
inner_payload_calls_multicall.checkpoint: during the outer batch, before the inner frame returns

inner_spends_eth_nonzero_msgvalue.meaning: the inner oracle update spends ETH with non-zero msgValue

followup_zero_value_call.meaning: a subsequent outer payload is a zero-value call
followup_zero_value_call.checkpoint: after the inner multicall frame returns, still inside the outer batch

batch_completes_without_incorrect_paymen.meaning: the top-level batch completes successfully without reverting with E_IncorrectPayment
batch_completes_without_incorrect_paymen.checkpoint: at completion of the top-level multicall batch

assumptions: The batch is solvent; the report states solvency as a condition rather than an observed prior state.
The caller is an integrator composing helper contracts; the report does not claim the caller is unauthorized.
Exact msgValue/msg.value numeric values are not given and are not needed for this qualitative liveness claim.

unresolved.description: Report states solvency as a condition ('even when solvent') rather than an observed prior state; the solvency predicate is not bound as a P term.

limitations: The impact is formalized as a liveness/composability failure (batch cannot complete without E_IncorrectPayment revert); the separate composability_break and user_facing_regression impacts are not covered by this plan.
The E_IncorrectPayment revert is represented as the absence of successful batch completion rather than a numeric payment comparison, since no msgValue/msg.value values are reported.
